analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. It changes docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 47-54) and docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 329). It documents a load-time "shape warmup" for standalone `--local` preload and adds the `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP` environment variable (disable values 0/false/no/off, `always` skips the probe, forwarded to the LaunchAgent). I examined the changes against T-041 (prefix cache and TTFT oracle), TB-007 (inference engine) and the TB-003 operator boundary. No source code, authentication, key handling, cache crypto, attestation or wire protocol changes are in the supplied evidence.

The docs state that the warmup trains no rate or counter, is excluded from serving, and is bounded to 20 seconds per engine. The warmup describes a 128-token shader-cache probe and shape cells. It is not stated to touch the prefix cache or write at-rest artifacts. Under T-041 that matters because a warmup that donated to the SSD prefix cache would need a new SEC-035 review. The docs do not claim that. They do say the sweep tick warms engines in the background and a request preempts it.

I could not verify the claims against the implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, architecture/inference.md) because that source is not supplied. Open integration questions for later passes:
- whether warmup input uses synthetic tokens and never enters the prefix cache or the SSD tier;
- whether the env-var forwarding to the LaunchAgent updates the passthrough allowlist in LaunchAgent.swift;
- whether the warmup does not alter timing-visible state beyond the accepted TTFT oracle.
No finding is warranted from the docs alone.
